packageRules.description: github.com/fyne-io/terminal is Cogpit's patched copy in third_party/fyne-terminal through a replace directive (D-14): an upstream update means syncing the copy by hand (third_party/fyne-terminal/PATCHES.md), so go.mod's require keeps naming the copy's base commit.

Go modules: every minor, patch and digest update in one pull request a week, so that CI runs once for them instead of once per module (owner, 2026-10-15: 21 pull requests at once flooded the shared runner node, GitHub refused the actions' downloads with 429 and none merged). Before the Go version rules, which keep golang.org/x/* with the Go version.
Go version: group all Go version updates together to keep them in sync (go.mod; the workflows read it through go-version-file)
Bundle golang.org/x/* updates with Go version bumps so govulncheck sees a consistent set (e.g. golang.org/x/net fixes shipped alongside Go releases)
Go version: automerge minor and patch updates after CI passes
Go version: require manual review for major updates
Go modules: enable updates for indirect dependencies so transitive security patches (e.g. golang.org/x/net via govulncheck) land without waiting for a direct require to bump
Go modules: automerge minor and patch updates after CI passes
Go modules: require manual review for major updates on direct requires

Go modules: never open major PRs for indirect deps. Module-path bumps (/v2 -> /v3) cannot be auto-applied without a direct importer, so go mod tidy resets the indirect line to the MVS minimum and Renovate keeps re-opening the same downgrade PR. Major updates land via the parent direct dependency.
GitHub Actions: automerge minor and patch updates
GitHub Actions: automerge major updates after CI passes
Makefile-pinned Go tools (custom regex manager): automerge minor and patch updates
Makefile-pinned Go tools (custom regex manager): require manual review for major updates

The node shell's default image (internal/engine/nodeshell.go, D-37): a new digest or a new Alpine release merges on its own once CI passes, whose kind job opens a node shell with it (TestKindNodeShell) and whose tests take the image from the constant; a major (Alpine 4) waits for review. It runs privileged as root on the node, which is why it is pinned by digest and the change is a pull request, never a floating tag.

The debug container's default image (internal/engine/debugcontainer.go, D-102): a new digest or a new netshoot release (v0.16 to v0.17, a minor update) merges on its own once CI passes, whose kind job adds a debug container with it, attaches and reads its log (TestKindDebugContainer); a major (v1) waits for review. It runs as root beside a pod's processes, which is why it is pinned by digest and the change is a pull request, never a floating tag.

Sparkle, the macOS app's updater (Makefile SPARKLE_VERSION, D-4), and WinSparkle, the Windows app's (WINSPARKLE_TAG, D-111): Renovate writes the new version and the new archive's SHA-256 (the archive pinned by version and digest, below), so nobody pushes onto its branch; their code updates installed copies, so a person reads the changes and merges the pull request, never Renovate on its own

Mesa for Windows (Makefile MESA_VERSION, D-142): pinned by version and the archive's SHA-256, which Renovate writes. A release cogpit.exe offers to download it on a computer without an OpenGL to draw with and loads it into its process, so a person reads the changes and merges the pull request, never Renovate on its own; the Windows Package job's smoke test draws with the new release

dmgbuild and its dependencies (hack/macos/dmgbuild-requirements.txt, D-70), pinned with their hashes: they make the template of the disk image's window in the app's job, outside the signing job, but their output ships in every disk image, so a person reads the changes and never merges them on their own. If Renovate cannot write the new hashes, take them from PyPI (https://pypi.org/pypi/<name>/<version>/json, the wheel's sha256).
Group Kubernetes-related Go dependencies
Group Fyne and its own modules (fyne.io/*, github.com/fyne-io/*): the toolkit, its terminal widget and the packaging tool move together

k8s.io/kube-openapi, sigs.k8s.io/structured-merge-diff and sigs.k8s.io/kustomize/* are indirect deps whose compatible version is dictated by the k8s.io/apimachinery release branch, not by their own tip. Renovate's digest updates advanced kube-openapi past the commit where it switched to structured-merge-diff/v7, which apimachinery v0.37.x cannot compile against; kustomize/api and kyaml v0.21.3 require that kube-openapi too (2026-10-12). Let MVS pick them from apimachinery, kubectl and Helm; they still advance whenever the k8s.io/* group does.

github.com/godbus/dbus/v5 v5.2.3 does not compile on macOS and Windows (conn_darwin.go and conn_windows.go: not enough return values; 2026-10-12). Fyne's systray imports it on every platform. Skip that version; a later one is tried as usual.

github.com/fyne-io/terminal is replaced by the patched copy in third_party/fyne-terminal, so bumping its require line changes no code and would only make go.mod name a base the copy is not on. Its update is the signal to move the copy onto that upstream commit (third_party/fyne-terminal/PATCHES.md); never automerge it.
Dependency updates are 'build(deps)', which semantic-release does not release: they ship with the next feat or fix (owner, 2026-10-13, docs/developer/releasing.md#renovate)
GitHub Actions: use 'chore' instead of 'fix' for updates

customManagers.description: Update Go tool versions pinned in Makefile via renovate comments. The value may be a release or a Go pseudo-version (vX.Y.Z-0.<time>-<commit>), which semver orders below the next release, so a tool pinned to an upstream commit moves onto that release on its own.

The node shell's default image (D-37, owner 2026-10-14): the newest supported Alpine release pinned by the digest of its multi-arch index, DefaultNodeShellImage in internal/engine/nodeshell.go under a renovate comment. A new Alpine release moves the tag (3.24 to 3.25, a minor update), a rebuilt tag moves the digest.

The debug container's default image (D-102, owner 2026-10-19): nicolaka/netshoot pinned by the digest of its multi-arch index, DefaultDebugImage in internal/engine/debugcontainer.go under a renovate comment. A new netshoot release moves the tag (v0.16 to v0.17), a rebuilt tag moves the digest; CI's kind job runs it (TestKindDebugContainer).

A release archive pinned by version and SHA-256 in the Makefile (Sparkle, D-4; WinSparkle, D-111; Mesa, D-142): a renovate comment with datasource=github-release-attachments, the release's tag on the next line (NAME := 2.10.0, or v0.9.4 where the tags carry a v) and the archive's SHA-256 on the one after (NAME_SHA256 := <64 hex digits>). The datasource looks up the release by that tag, finds the asset whose SHA-256 is the pinned one and hashes the asset of the same name in the new release, so the update changes both lines and needs no commit of anyone else on Renovate's branch (a branch someone else pushed to is never rebased by Renovate again and stays in conflict, PR #110).
